subject: Discovery recap & quick question on Q3 relevance
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.in>
To: Evan Williamson <evan@williamson-analytics.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@williamson-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.in>
Date: Wed, Jul 1 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & quick question on Q3 relevance

Thanks again for the time today — quick written recap so we’re aligned and so you have a single artifact to share internally.

Key takeaways from today’s call:
- Primary use case: real-time invoice reconciliation & free-text extraction from vendor attachments for the AP team.
- Current pain: throughput latency on batch OCR + manual reconciliation steps -> 2–3 FTEs.
- Success metric: reduce manual review time by >=50% and lower per-invoice processing cost by 40% for Q4 pilot.
- Security requirement: data residency in US, SOC2 evidence required, encrypted-at-rest with KMS.

What Redwood would recommend next (high level):
1) Pilot (6 weeks): hosted API POC using 2 models (one accuracy-focused, one quantized for latency) to validate end-to-end latency and accuracy on a small invoice sample.
2) Measurements: per-invoice latency, accuracy on line-item extraction, and cost-per-invoice.
3) If pilot meets thresholds -> Dedicated pool for sustained throughput + VPC connectivity for production.

Next steps / ask from Williamson:
- Does the pilot timeline (target start in Q3) still match your roadmap?
- Can you share one representative invoice sample (anonymized) and the internal SLA you’d need?

Attachments: 20260701-williamson-discovery-deck.pdf (PDF) — short deck summarizing the pilot approach and success criteria.

If it’s easier, we can do a 15-minute sync next week to iron timing — Monica (cc) can walk the team through caching and batching options that typically cut token spend by 25–40%.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
